title: Aviation Logistician (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6002, 6302, 6502, 6602), DC AVN
raw_text:
3. MOS 6607, Aviation Logistician (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO)
NMOS (6002, 6302, 6502, 6602), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Logisticians are assigned to selected headquarters
and staffs. They are trained in aviation logistics (AVLOG) support plan
development. The skill set provides headquarters staffs with aviation
logistics specific subject matter expertise to support the force deployment
planning and execution process, exercise planning, pre-positioning program
development execution, and doctrine development.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) Must possess PMOSs 6002, Aircraft Maintenance Officer, MOS 6004,
Aircraft Maintenance Engineer Officer, MOS 6302, Avionics Officer, MOS 6502,
Aviation Ordnance Officer, MOS 6602, Aviation Supply Officer, or MOS 6604,
Aviation Supply Operations Officer.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete at least two of the following courses:

            (a) Joint Logistics Course (JLC) (A14L232) at the U.S. Army
Logistics University (ALU), Ft Gregg-Adams, VA.

            (b) Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) Action
Officer Course (JAOC) (JD2101) at Ft Eustis, VA.

            (c) Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES)
Support Personnel Course (JSPC) (JD1102) at Ft Eustis, VA.




                                         1-252                        Enclosure (1)
 1138                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (d) Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) Staff Planning Course,
covered by the Expeditionary Warfare Training Group (CIN: K-2E-3119) or
(N03L8Q1 or N30L8Q1).

       d.   Duties

        (1) Serve as AVLOG representative for operational planning teams and
crisis action teams.

        (2) Support the development, review, and update of OPLANS/CONPLANS in
support of higher headquarters' directives.

        (3) Review/validate time phased force deployment data to ensure
compliance with guidance and directives.

            (4) Develop estimates of supportability and concepts of logistics
support.

        (5) Support the development and operational orders and letters of
instruction for ACE operations and exercises.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

            (2) Administrative Services Managers 11-3011.

            (3) Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

            (4) Logisticians 13-1081.

            (5) Operations Research Analysts 15-2031.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
